The DAC sorbent (Figure 1) consists of a polymer backbone that is resistant to water adsorption, a functionalized amine and promoter that can achieve high CO adsorption 2 capacity and rate and is resistant to oxidative degradation during sorbent regeneration from steam and/or oxygen present during sorbent regeneration and cooldown. Figure 1. Sorbent design criteria The structured sorbent filter consists of the CO sorbent coated onto a nonwoven filter substrate that can be 2 heated directly via joule heating. The nonwoven filter design allows for high air flow throughput with minimal pressure drop (<100 Pa). The filter substrate is electrically conductive, which allows for direct, rapid electric heating for efficient sorbent regeneration/CO production. The filter substrate also has low 2 thermal mass, representing <10wt% of the total mass of the structured sorbent assembly, resulting in minimal parasitic energy loss for heating the filter substrate. The structured sorbent filter can be manufactured using the existing infrastructure used to manufacture air purification filters, reducing the risk of scale-up of the structured sorbent filter. 1.2. Technology Readiness Level The current technology readiness level (TRL) for Susteon’s DAC technology is TRL 4. Component or system validation in laboratory environment is complete, and the technology is ready for TRL 5 – prototype demonstration in a simulated environment. At the completion of the current project, Susteon’s DAC filter technology has undergone the following development highlights and is primed for progression to TRL 5 and beyond: 1. Selection and validation of DAC sorbent with high working capacity (>5wt%) and adsorption rate that has good oxidative stability 2. Successfully scaled sorbent synthesis process to produce 50 kg of ECCOSorb-T1 3. Selection of an electrically conductive nonwoven filter substrate capable of direct Joule heating 4. Validation from commercial filter manufacturing partner the structured sorbent assembly can be manufactured using their existing filter manufacturing infrastructure. 5. Demonstrated the structured sorbent filter operation for DAC with Joule-heated regeneration. 1.2.1 Sorbent Development The result of the materials development work was Susteon’s ECCOSorb-T1 formulation, a balance between high performance and stability to reduce the overall cost of CO removal from air. The optimized sorbent 2 achieved a working capacity of 1.14 mmol CO captured per gram of sorbent (5 wt%) in about 26 minutes, 2 corresponding to an average capture capacity of 0.04 mmol/g-min.
